summary: Yancey County, NC summit lookout: wooden platform 1916, steel tower blown down 1925, stone tower opened 1927; later replaced, and a visitor deck stands today.

facts.design: Stone tower designed in a medieval motif, opened on the summit in 1927 as a memorial to Elisha Mitchell
facts.status_note: The 1927 stone tower was torn down; the summit now has a visitor observation deck that the state park describes as a viewing deck, not a fire lookout.
facts.ownership: state park land (Mount Mitchell State Park); summit surrounded by Pisgah National Forest lands

access.note: State park open to visitors. Winter closures can be frequent and prolonged. Reached by NC 128 from the Blue Ridge Parkway, then a paved trail to the summit.

visit.trail_note: Steep paved trail of about 980 feet (300 m) from the parking lot to the summit

events.note: Covered wooden platform about 15 feet high, built when Mount Mitchell State Park was established. A 1923-24 state report calls the earlier tower sixteen feet tall.

Per the 1923-24 biennial report, a contract was entered into with a manufacturer for a steel tower, and an agreement was made with the National Forest Service to share the cost. The tower was to carry a watchman's cottage and an observation platform thirty feet above the summit and to be staffed by a Forest Service watchman in the spring and fall fire seasons.

Steel tower reported blown down by heavy winds in January 1925; the Asheville Citizen-Times described it as 35 feet high. A 1925-26 state report says it was erected in fall 1925, which conflicts with a January 1925 collapse.

Stone tower built in 1926 with a medieval motif, replacing the wooden platform (FHS). Opened and dedicated on June 17, 1927 as a memorial to Elisha Mitchell (Forest Lookouts quoting The Forest Worker, 1927).
Described in 1927 as about 35 feet high and meant as an outlook for detecting and reporting forest fires, used by the U.S. Forest Service and the state conservation department.
Stone tower torn down in 1959 (CLUI). The Forest History Society says the stone tower was replaced in 1959.
A new architect-designed tower that incorporated the stone tower's original form, with a larger viewing platform, opened in 1960 (CLUI).
The 1960 successor was removed in 2006 and replaced by a platform about ten feet high (CLUI). Wikipedia says the 40-foot stone observation tower was torn down in late 2006.
New observation deck constructed and opened to visitors in January 2009 (Wikipedia). The Forest History Society calls it a handicap-accessible observation deck.

corrections.why: The Forest Lookouts page says the summit is included in Mount Mitchell State Park and only surrounded by Pisgah National Forest lands. The summit tower site is state park land, not federal.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The 1927 notice says about 35 feet, which matches the record's 10.7 m. Wikipedia gives a 40-foot (12 m) stone observation tower torn down in late 2006. The sources do not say whether that tower is the 1927 structure or its 1960 successor, so the story gives 35 feet for the 1925 steel tower and the 1927 stone tower, and says the 35-foot and 40-foot figures may describe different structures.

The Forest History Society says the stone tower was replaced in 1959 and the next tower in 2009. CLUI says the stone tower was torn down in 1959, a 1960 successor was removed in 2006 and a platform replaced it. Wikipedia gives late 2006 for the 40-foot tower's removal and January 2009 for the new deck. The story follows CLUI for 1959, 1960 and 2006, the Forest History Society for the 2009 replacement of the 1959 tower, and Wikipedia for the January 2009 deck. It does not say whether CLUI's ten-foot platform is that deck.

The 1925-26 state report says the steel tower was erected in fall 1925, yet it also says the tower collapsed in January 1925. The Asheville Citizen-Times reported the blow-down in January 1925. The story gives both the January 1925 collapse and the report's fall 1925 erection date, and says the sources disagree on the dates.

The Forest History Society says the 1916 wooden platform was about 15 feet high. The 1923-24 state report says the wooden tower was sixteen feet. The story gives 15 feet attributed to the Forest History Society and mentions the report's figure.
The 1925-26 report names Col. C.J. Harris of Hillsboro, and the 1927 notice gives Dillsboro. The story does not name a town.

sources.title: Mt. Mitchell, Where Mystery, Intrigue, and Forest History Meet!

notes_for_editor: The lookout history rests on Forest Lookouts' transcripts of 1920s state biennial reports and newspapers, the Forest History Society essay, CLUI and Wikipedia. The sources conflict on dates for the 1925 steel tower, the 1959/1960/2006 removals and the 2009 deck, and on height (35 ft in 1927 vs 40 ft in Wikipedia). Check the 1959, 1960 and 2006 dates against the NC State Archives file 'Documents regarding the construction of a stone watchtower at Mount Mitchell State Park, 1925-1927' (NC Digital Collections item 373257); that page returned no readable text during research. The Forest History Society also gives a 1928 date for a permanent plaque at Elisha Mitchell's grave; the story leaves that out because it is not the tower's history. The record's ownership was 'federal' in an earlier draft; the story now says state park land, as the corrections entry proposes. The summit observation deck is not a fire lookout; the visit note is for visitors, not a climbing route. Two web searches were used.
